solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outside university prepare for threats

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is a mass noun for the same thing

indicators.note: the word for prepare sits on the outside, wrapping the abbreviation for university

blocks.note: to dress is to prepare, as with a salad or a wound

explanation.surface: Students outside a university brace themselves against threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure applied through menaces, so threats used to force someone amount to it.

clue.text: Individual with record time raking in the money

indicators.note: raking in money means gathering it inside, so the record takes the cash word within it

explanation.surface: A solo artist with a record-breaking hit is making a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for cash; the money sits inside the record before time is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Individual, as an adjective, means separate and distinguishable from others, the sense of distinct.

clue.text: They offer contrary evidence and sure fret when shown to be wrong

indicators.note: letters shown to be wrong are in the wrong order, so they need rearranging

explanation.surface: Debaters bring counter-evidence, and a confident man frets once proven mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute is to disprove, so refuters are people who produce evidence against a claim.

clue.text: Sound odd when going after holy woman?

indicators.note: the odd word is placed after the holy woman's abbreviation

blocks.note: rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: Something seems strange when a man chases after a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum a guitar is to sound its strings by sweeping fingers across them.

clue.text: I had backed minister, as one of the bosses

indicators.note: something backed is put in reverse, so the short form of I had runs right to left

blocks.note: a rector is a parish minister

explanation.surface: Someone recalls supporting a churchman who sat on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A company director sits on the board, so is one of the people in charge of a business.

clue.text: Liaisons? To sit out might suit them

definitions.text: Liaisons? To sit out might suit them

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the preceding letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: People who shun alliances would happily sit out any liaisons.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: those who keep their nation out of foreign alliances would be glad to sit them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolationists oppose foreign entanglements and alliances, preferring their country to stay apart from others.

clue.text: Being one with a history of being loved, is joining number going to church

indicators.note: going to means added onto, so the church abbreviation is attached last

blocks.clueFragment: one with a history of being loved

explanation.surface: A former lover, now one of a congregation, joins the churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: An ex is a former partner, someone once loved. The Church of England is routinely shortened to its two initials in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Being, as a noun, means the state of living or being real, which is existence.

clue.text: Pain shown by women in flush?

indicators.note: the letter for women is placed inside the word for a flush

blocks.note: a tinge of colour in the cheeks

explanation.surface: Discomfort is suggested by a woman's blush.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pain, so it is a short burst of hurt.

clue.text: Furious student event with booze being imbibed

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the booze goes inside the student event

blocks.note: a rag is a British student charity fundraising event

explanation.surface: An angry student party where the drink flows freely.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is when British university students run stunts to raise money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging describes intense, violent anger, so someone furious could be called raging.

clue.text: Female in the ascent up to now

indicators.note: the letter for female is placed inside the word for the climb

blocks.note: a soar is an upward flight

explanation.surface: A woman is taking part in a climb that has gone well so far.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase so far means until the present moment, as in nothing has gone wrong yet.

clue.text: I perform as musician at end of concert, as an up-and-coming artist?

definitions.note: describes the answer: an artist who shows great potential is so described

indicators.note: the performing phrase comes after the concert word, placed at its end

blocks.note: a Prom is one of the BBC's Promenade Concerts in London
a musician performing might say 'I sing'

explanation.surface: A young performer sings at the close of a concert and is hailed as a rising talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer series of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist on the way up shows potential for future success, which is what promising means.

clue.text: Team's stopgaps being trained — they don't get licked the way they used to be

definitions.text: they don't get licked the way they used to be

indicators.note: being trained means being reshaped and put through drills, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A sports team's reserve players are coached, though they aren't thrashed as they once were.
explanation.walkthrough: Licked looks like beaten in a sporting sense; stamps were once moistened with the tongue but are now self-adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage stamps used to have gummed backs that people wet with their tongues; modern ones are mostly self-sticking.

clue.text: Land with sea either side – this ground mostly soft pulpy stuff?

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the word this is rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the pulp word is dropped

explanation.surface: A geographer wonders whether a narrow neck of land is mostly soggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip connecting two larger landmasses, with water on both of its flanks.

clue.text: Biological substance with which lady ensnares cat without tail

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the lady's name holds the cat inside it
the last letter of the big cat is removed

explanation.surface: A woman traps a cat whose tail is missing, in some lab sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady is any woman's name here; the cat is the tiger, and it must lose its final letter before going in.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a molecule that triggers the immune system to produce antibodies, a substance studied in biology.

clue.text: Connection made with member of family getting expression of surprise at first

indicators.note: the exclamation comes first, before the family member

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: Someone is linked by marriage to a family member who gasps in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A correlation is a mutual relationship or link between two things, such as variables in statistics.

clue.text: Impression of English — mad?

explanation.surface: It reads as asking whether the general view of the English is that they are crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a print taken from an incised plate, an impression in the printing sense.

clue.text: Miss more when looking, being innocent

blocks.note: first meaning, split in two: to see fewer things, read as a phrase
second meaning: pure, without a stain

explanation.surface: Someone who notices less while searching is held to be blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read as two words: if you miss more, you notice less.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without a mark or blemish, figuratively free of guilt, so blameless and pure.

clue.text: Support the man's yen to be a Jeremiah?

explanation.surface: Someone backs a man's longing to become a doom-monger.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremiah was the Old Testament prophet of doom, so his name stands for anyone forecasting disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a Jeremiah means foretelling calamity, and to prophesy is to predict future events.

clue.text: Groundsman, inexperienced fellow on the cricket field?

blocks.note: on a cricket field the keeper is the wicketkeeper, the fielder behind the stumps

explanation.surface: A raw young player takes the field at a cricket match, or tends the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket field reference is what turns fellow into a wicketkeeper; it also points at the ground staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenkeeper looks after the turf of a golf course or bowling green, as a groundsman does.

clue.text: Short and thickset agent with stomach to hide

indicators.note: the agent conceals the stomach word by holding it inside

explanation.surface: A squat secret agent tries to conceal his paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpy means short and thick like a stump, so it describes a squat, stocky build.

clue.text: Brief comment from a copper for each getting nabbed

indicators.note: nabbed means caught and held, so the each word is held inside the copper phrase

blocks.note: A plus CU, the chemical symbol for copper
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: A police officer makes a terse remark as each suspect is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a short insightful remark or summary, so it is a brief comment or glimpse.

clue.text: One policeman that's keen to get around in vehicle

indicators.note: the keen word goes around the one and the policeman, enclosing them

blocks.note: tart means sharp, as keen does

explanation.surface: An eager police officer is keen to drive about in a patrol car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-cart is a cart whose body can be tilted to dump its load, so it is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Separated, without children, and animated

blocks.note: sp, Latin sine prole, is used in family trees for dying without issue
lit up means lively, glowing with excitement

explanation.surface: A childless couple parted and became cheerful again.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is a genealogists' abbreviation for sine prole, without offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have split up have ended their relationship and gone their own ways, apart.

clue.text: The French getting sick in one of their cities

indicators.note: the French article gets, that is takes in, the sick word

blocks.note: the masculine definite article in French

explanation.surface: The French fall ill in one of their own cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France near the Belgian border, so it is a French city.

clue.text: Flaw with matins arranged for saint's day

indicators.note: arranged suggests the morning prayers word is put in a fresh order

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or flaw

explanation.surface: A clergyman spoils the morning service planned for a saint's feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinmas is the feast of St Martin of Tours on 11 November, a saint's day in the church calendar.

clue.text: The province of sovereign or subject

blocks.note: first meaning: a province, and its city, in eastern Belgium
second meaning: in feudal usage the word names both a lord and his vassal

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question of whose domain a matter falls within: the ruler's or the subject's.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a Belgian province, and in feudal law a liege can be either the overlord or the vassal owing him loyalty.

clue.text: Unfortunate guy set on as the most junior

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unlucky chap is picked on because he is the newest recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest person in a group has the lowest age, so is the most junior member.

clue.text: Indeed, dirty place may be restless and turbulent

blocks.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
a pigsty, the byword for filth

explanation.surface: A grimy spot may indeed be a scene of unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast makes liquid froth and ferment, so yeasty describes something agitated, frothy and unsettled.
